models.description:
Overview
This is an XGBoost binary classifier trained to predict presence of heart disease from clinical and demographic features.

Training Data
Trained on the Heart Failure Prediction Dataset (918 rows, 11 features), which combines five heart disease datasets (Cleveland, Hungary, Switzerland, VA, Stalog). Features include age, sex, chest pain type, resting blood pressure, cholesterol, fasting blood sugar, resting ECG, max heart rate, exercise-induced angina, oldpeak, and ST slope. Target is binary: heart disease present (1) or absent (0).
Model Details

Algorithm: XGBoost (XGBClassifier)
Hyperparameters: n_estimators=100, max_depth=3, learning_rate=0.1
No hyperparameter tuning applied this is a baseline model
Data was already numeric/pre-encoded, so no additional preprocessing pipeline was required

Performance

Single train/test split (80/20, stratified): 97.6% accuracy, 97.6% balanced accuracy
5-fold stratified cross-validation (more reliable estimate): 95.8% mean balanced accuracy (std dev 0.022)
Recall on positive class (disease present): 0.97 model misses roughly 3% of true disease cases

Limitations

Small dataset (918 rows) means performance estimates have some variance across folds (std ~0.022)
No hyperparameter tuning performed this is an untuned baseline
Not validated on external/out-of-distribution clinical data
Not intended for real clinical or diagnostic use this is an educational/portfolio project

Intended Use
Educational demonstration of XGBoost for tabular binary classification. Not for medical decision-making.

instances.overview: Baseline XGBoost classifier (n_estimators=100, max_depth=3, learning_rate=0.1), untuned. Trained on 80% of the Heart Failure Prediction dataset (918 rows), stratified split. Achieves 95.8% mean balanced accuracy across 5-fold stratified cross-validation (std 0.022), with 0.97 recall on the positive (disease present) class. Input features: Age, Sex, ChestPainType, RestingBP, Cholesterol, FastingBS, RestingECG, MaxHR, ExerciseAngina, Oldpeak, ST_Slope all pre-encoded as numeric. Saved via model.save_model() in XGBoost's native JSON format.

import xgboost as xgb
import pandas as pd

model = xgb.XGBClassifier()
model.load_model('heart_disease_xgb_model.json')

new_patient = pd.DataFrame([{
    'Age': 54, 'Sex': 1, 'ChestPainType': 2, 'RestingBP': 130,
    'Cholesterol': 246, 'FastingBS': 0, 'RestingECG': 0,
    'MaxHR': 150, 'ExerciseAngina': 0, 'Oldpeak': 1.2, 'ST_Slope': 1
}])

prediction = model.predict(new_patient)
probability = model.predict_proba(new_patient)

print("Prediction (1=disease, 0=no disease):", prediction[0])
print("Probability:", probability[0])
}

models.provenanceSources:
This model was created from scratch by training an XGBoost classifier on the publicly available Heart Failure Prediction Dataset by fedesoriano on Kaggle, which itself combines five original heart disease datasets (Cleveland, Hungary, Switzerland, VA Long Beach, and Stalog) collected via clinical cardiology studies.
Training was performed independently: data was split 80/20 (stratified) for evaluation, with 5-fold stratified cross-validation used to confirm performance stability. No pretrained weights, existing model checkpoints, or third-party model artifacts were used — the model was trained end-to-end from the raw tabular data using xgboost.XGBClassifier with baseline (untuned) hyperparameters.
No external code, notebooks, or model files were copied; the preprocessing, training, and evaluation pipeline was written and run independently as part of a personal learning project.

# Description

SigLino is a family of vision foundation models developed by the Technology Innovation Institute (TII). The models are distilled from the complementary strengths of SigLIP2 and DINOv3, combining semantic image-text alignment with robust self-supervised visual representations. The project originates from the AMoE (Agglomerative Mixture-of-Experts) research and was accepted at CVPR 2026.

The SigLino collection includes both dense and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) vision encoders designed for image feature extraction, image retrieval, zero-shot image classification, semantic segmentation, multimodal retrieval, and vision-language applications. The models generate multiple feature representations, including SigLino, SigLIP2, and DINOv3 embeddings, making them highly flexible for downstream computer vision and multimodal AI tasks.

This collection contains lightweight 30M, 70M, 0.6B Dense, and 0.6B MoE models, allowing users to choose between maximum efficiency and maximum accuracy. By default, this repository uses SigLino-0.6B, providing the best balance between performance and computational efficiency for most vision applications.

The models are fully compatible with PyTorch and Hugging Face Transformers, enabling deployment on Kaggle, local systems, research environments, and production computer vision pipelines.

License: Apache License 2.0.

Included Models

| Model                      |                Parameters | Architecture |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------: | ------------ |
| SigLino-30M                |                       30M | Dense        |
| SigLino-70M                |                       70M | Dense        |
| **SigLino-0.6B (Default)** |                      0.6B | Dense        |
| SigLino-MoE-0.15-0.6B      | 0.6B Total (0.15B Active) | MoE          |
| SigLino-MoE-0.3-0.6B       |  0.6B Total (0.3B Active) | MoE          |

**Key Features**
Vision foundation models distilled from SigLIP2 and DINOv3
Dense and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures
Models from 30M to 0.6B parameters
Multi-resolution image understanding
Image feature extraction
Image retrieval and similarity search
Zero-shot image classification
Semantic segmentation support
Vision-language feature extraction
Compatible with PyTorch and Hugging Face Transformers
Fine-tunable for downstream computer vision tasks

## Model Summary

SigLino combines the semantic understanding capabilities of SigLIP2 with the robust visual representations learned by DINOv3 to create efficient vision encoders for a wide variety of downstream tasks. The collection offers compact dense models for efficient inference and MoE variants for improved scalability, making it suitable for image retrieval, classification, multimodal AI, and large-scale visual understanding. SigLino-0.6B is recommended as the default model for general-purpose vision applications.

## Usage

SigLino models are designed for image feature extraction, image retrieval, zero-shot image classification, semantic segmentation, multimodal retrieval, visual search, representation learning, and downstream computer vision applications. By default, this collection loads SigLino-0.6B. Other variants can be selected by changing the model directory.

## Disclaimer

***Disclaimer:*** The **Technology Innovation Institute (TII)** and original owners/authors of the model completely reserve the right to contact us regarding the removal of the hosted model.

SigLino models are designed for image feature extraction, image retrieval, zero-shot image classification, semantic segmentation, multimodal retrieval, visual search, representation learning, and downstream computer vision applications. By default, this collection loads SigLino-0.6B. Other variants can be selected by changing the model directory.

from transformers import AutoModel, AutoImageProcessor
from PIL import Image
import torch

model_path = "/kaggle/input/siglino/siglino-0.6b"

processor = AutoImageProcessor.from_pretrained(
    model_path,
    trust_remote_code=True
)

model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(
    model_path,
    trust_remote_code=True,
    torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
    device_map="auto"
)

image = Image.open("image.jpg").convert("RGB")

inputs = processor(image, return_tensors="pt").to(model.device)
inputs["pixel_values"] = inputs["pixel_values"].to(torch.bfloat16)

with torch.no_grad():
    outputs = model(**inputs)

features = outputs["summary_features"]["siglino"]
print(features.shape)

models.description:
# Model Summary

LoRA adapter for hierarchical classification of CFPB consumer complaint
narratives, fine-tuned on **Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1** (46.7B total
parameters, 12.9B active per token — sparse mixture-of-experts) via
[Adaption's](https://adaptionlabs.ai) AutoScientist platform. Given a
consumer complaint narrative, the model assigns a three-level label from
the CFPB taxonomy — **Product → Issue → Sub-issue** — where each level is
constrained to be valid under its parent.

This is **closed-label classification**, not open generation: the output
space is a fixed taxonomy of 393 valid triples, and a correct answer is one
of those triples. Anything outside the taxonomy is a label hallucination.

Submitted to the **AutoScientist Challenge 2026** (Personal Finance category).

## Usage

This is a LoRA adapter. Load it on top of the base model using PEFT. Because
training used `data_format="chat"`, wrap the narrative as a user turn via the
tokenizer's chat template — raw text will not match the training format.

```python
import torch
from peft import PeftModel
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer

base = "mistralai/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1"
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(base)
base_model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
    base, torch_dtype=torch.float16, device_map="auto",
)
model = PeftModel.from_pretrained(
    base_model,
    "/kaggle/input/cfpb-consumer-finance-complaints-adapter/other/default/1",
)

SYSTEM = (
    "Classify the CFPB consumer complaint into exactly one Product, one "
    "Issue nested under it, and one Sub-issue nested under that Issue. "
    "Output the three labels verbatim from the CFPB taxonomy, three lines, "
    "no explanation."
)
narrative = (
    "I opened a checking account online and changed my direct deposit to it. "
    "Two weeks later the bank closed the account without notice and I cannot "
    "access the funds."
)

# CRITICAL: data_format was 'chat'. Wrap as a user turn via the chat template.
messages = [{"role": "user", "content": f"{SYSTEM}\n\nComplaint:\n{narrative}"}]
inputs = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
    messages, add_generation_prompt=True, return_tensors="pt",
).to(model.device)
outputs = model.generate(inputs, max_new_tokens=64, do_sample=False)
print(tokenizer.decode(outputs[0][inputs.shape[-1]:], skip_special_tokens=True))

# Expected:
# Product: Checking or savings account
# Issue: Closing an account
# Sub-issue: Company closed your account
```

**Input:** A task instruction plus one consumer complaint narrative in English.
**Output:** Three lines — `Product:`, `Issue:`, `Sub-issue:` — with labels
drawn verbatim from the CFPB taxonomy.

**Known limitations:** The adapter is domain-specialized and trades general
capability for in-domain accuracy (see the Legal cross-domain drop under
Evaluation Results). Outputs are automated and require review before any
operational use.

## System

Standalone LoRA adapter. Requires the base model
`mistralai/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1` to be loaded first via PEFT.

## Implementation requirements

- **Training platform:** Adaption AutoScientist (cloud compute)
- **Base model size:** 46.7B total parameters / 12.9B active per token
  (sparse mixture-of-experts)
- **Training method:** SFT + LoRA (all-linear modules)
- **Training epochs:** 5
- **Inference:** Requires GPU with enough VRAM to hold Mixtral's full
  46.7B-parameter footprint (sparse activation reduces compute, not memory —
  all experts must be resident). 4-bit quantization fits on ~24 GB.

---

# Model Characteristics

## Model initialization

Fine-tuned from `mistralai/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1` using LoRA. Base model
weights are frozen; only the LoRA adapter weights are trained.

## Model stats

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Base model | Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1 |
| Base model size | 46.7B parameters (12.9B active per token) |
| LoRA rank (r) | 64 |
| LoRA alpha | 128 |
| LoRA dropout | 0 |
| Trainable modules | all-linear |
| Learning rate | 1e-4 (cosine, warmup 0.05) |
| Weight decay | 0.05 |
| Train on inputs | false |
| Data format | chat |

---

# Data Overview

## Training data

**Dataset:** [adaption-consumer-finance-complaints (HF)](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Fernandosr85/adaption-consumer-finance-complaints)
· **Diagnostic:** [CFPB Zero-Shot Baseline (Kaggle)](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/fernandosr85/cfpb-zero-shot-baseline-closed-label-diagnostic)

12,346 prompt/completion pairs, built from the full CFPB Consumer Complaint
Database with a deliberate methodology:

| Step | Detail |
|---|---|
| Taxonomy vintage | Fixed at the 2023-08-25 consolidation (11 current Products) |
| Deduplication | 52.1% of post-2023 narratives are exact duplicates after normalization; removed |
| Rebalance | Credit reporting falls 72.6% → 46.2% of the corpus after dedup |
| Split | Temporal (train < 2025-07, eval = July 2025) |
| Registry | 393 valid triples, derived from **train only** |
| Hard negatives | Boosted from a measured product-confusion matrix |
| Completions | Kept verbatim from the taxonomy, **not** platform-regenerated |

The output space is 11 Products × 86 Issues × 209 Sub-issues ≈ 197,714
unconstrained combinations; the hierarchy reduces this to 393 valid triples,
a **503× reduction**.

## Evaluation data

Evaluation performed by Adaption AutoScientist on held-out internal test sets
for the Personal Finance category. A separate 742-row temporal holdout (July
2025) is published in the diagnostic dataset for independent baseline
comparison; the July window is the last month at the stable publication
plateau, before CFPB narrative publication collapsed in late 2025.

---

# Evaluation Results

## Summary — Adaption AutoScientist win rate

| Metric | Base | Adapted |
|---|---|---|
| Win rate — in-domain (this dataset) | 17 | **83** |
| Win rate — Legal reference category | 64 | 36 |

The in-domain gain is **+66 points**. The Legal drop (−28) is catastrophic
forgetting — expected for a task-specific adapter, reported for transparency.

## Context — zero-shot baselines on the CFPB taxonomy

For reference, on the published 742-row holdout, general-purpose and classical
baselines score as follows (triple exact-match / hallucination rate):

| Method | Triple exact-match | Hallucination |
|---|---|---|
| Majority-triple | 16.2% | 0% |
| Claude zero-shot (Sonnet) | 20.3% | 21.6% |
| TF-IDF + SGD (300k train) | 37.6% | 0% |

These establish the difficulty of the task: a frontier model given zero
examples hallucinates an invalid label 21.6% of the time, and a linear
classifier over 300k rows reaches 37.6% exact-match. The headroom is in
learning the Product → Issue → Sub-issue hierarchy, which is what this adapter
is trained to do.

## Usage limitations

- Domain-specialized. Not intended for general-purpose use (see Legal drop).
- Automated classification; requires review before operational use.

## Ethics

Built to reduce label hallucination in automated complaint routing — the
tendency of general-purpose LLMs to emit plausible but invalid labels, or to
attach a valid label under the wrong parent. All labels are grounded in the
public CFPB taxonomy. The training completions were kept verbatim rather than
platform-regenerated, precisely because regeneration introduced retired labels
(e.g. `Bank account or service`, removed by the CFPB in August 2023).

---

## Credits

- **Fine-tuning platform:** [Adaption](https://adaptionlabs.ai) — AutoScientist & Adaptive Data
- **Challenge:** [AutoScientist Challenge 2026](https://adaptionlabs.ai/blog/autoscientist-challenge) — Personal Finance category
- **Data source:** [CFPB Consumer Complaint Database](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/data-research/consumer-complaints/) (public)
- **HuggingFace model:** [consumer-finance-complaints-cfpb-adapter](https://huggingface.co/Fernandosr85/consumer-finance-complaints-cfpb-adapter)
- **HuggingFace dataset:** [adaption-consumer-finance-complaints](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Fernandosr85/adaption-consumer-finance-complaints)
- **Kaggle diagnostic:** [cfpb-zero-shot-baseline-closed-label-diagnostic](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/fernandosr85/cfpb-zero-shot-baseline-closed-label-diagnostic)
- **Author:** Fernando Rodrigues · [Kaggle: fernandosr85](https://www.kaggle.com/fernandosr85)

fine-tuned on Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct (46.7B total / 12.9B active parameters)
via Adaption AutoScientist — supervised fine-tuning, cosine LR schedule,
5 epochs. Trained on 12,346 CFPB consumer-complaint narratives, each labeled
with a three-level triple from the CFPB taxonomy: Product → Issue → Sub-issue.

The task is closed-label classification: 11 Products, 86 Issues, 209 Sub-issues,
393 valid triples against 197,714 unconstrained combinations — a 503× reduction
of the output space. Training data was deduplicated (52.1% of post-2023 narratives
are exact duplicates), stratified by (Product, Issue) pair, with hard negatives
drawn from a measured product-confusion matrix. Completions were kept verbatim
from the taxonomy, not platform-regenerated.

In-domain win rate: 17 → 83 (+66 points) via Adaption AutoScientist training.
Cross-domain tradeoff: Legal reference category drops 64 → 36 (catastrophic
forgetting, expected for a task-specific adapter).

Inference note: data_format was "chat"; wrap the narrative as a user turn via
the tokenizer chat template — raw text will not match the training format.

Licensed under Apache 2.0.

    base,
    torch_dtype=torch.float16,
    device_map="auto",
)

# Load adapter from Kaggle
model = PeftModel.from_pretrained(
    base_model,
    "/kaggle/input/cfpb-consumer-finance-complaints-adapter/other/default/1",
)

# The task instruction used during training (labels verbatim, no explanation)
SYSTEM = (
    "Classify the CFPB consumer complaint into exactly one Product, one "
    "Issue nested under it, and one Sub-issue nested under that Issue. "
    "Output the three labels verbatim from the CFPB taxonomy, three lines, "
    "no explanation."
)

narrative = (
    "I opened a checking account online and changed my direct deposit to it. "
    "Two weeks later the bank closed the account without notice and I cannot "
    "access the funds. No one can tell me why the account was closed or where "
    "my money is."
)

# CRITICAL: data_format was 'chat'. Wrap as a user turn via the chat template.
# Feeding raw text with tokenizer(prompt) will NOT match the training format.
messages = [{"role": "user", "content": f"{SYSTEM}\n\nComplaint:\n{narrative}"}]
inputs = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
    messages,
    add_generation_prompt=True,
    return_tensors="pt",
).to(model.device)

outputs = model.generate(inputs, max_new_tokens=64, do_sample=False)
print(tokenizer.decode(outputs[0][inputs.shape[-1]:], skip_special_tokens=True))

# Expected output:
# Product: Checking or savings account
# Issue: Closing an account
# Sub-issue: Company closed your account

models.provenanceSources:
Fine-tuned from mistralai/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1 using Adaption
AutoScientist platform. Training data: 12,346 CFPB consumer-complaint
narratives, each labeled with a Product → Issue → Sub-issue triple from
the CFPB taxonomy (11 Products, 86 Issues, 209 Sub-issues, 393 valid
triples). Source: CFPB Consumer Complaint Database (public,
files.consumerfinance.gov). Taxonomy fixed at the 2023-08-25 consolidation
cutoff; deduplicated (52.1% of post-2023 narratives are exact duplicates);
stratified by (Product, Issue) pair with hard negatives from a measured
confusion matrix. Completions kept verbatim from the taxonomy, not
platform-regenerated. SFT + LoRA (r=64, alpha=128, all-linear), 5 epochs,
data_format=chat.
